name: open
description: Open a GitHub pull request. Defaults to the branch the workspace is on, against the repository's own default branch. The branch must already be pushed: nothing in these packs pushes for you.

body.description: The description, as markdown. Optional, but a pull request opened by a flow should say what produced it.

source.description: The branch to merge from. Omit to use the branch the workspace is on.

target.description: The branch to merge into. Omit to use the repository's own default branch, which is read from the API rather than assumed to be "main".

draft.description: Open it as a draft. Worth doing when a flow opened it and a person has not read it yet.

repo.description: The repository as "owner/name". Omit to read it from the workspace's origin remote.

output_schema.description: The pull request that was opened. `number` and `url` are what a later step needs; the rest is what was actually recorded, which is not always what was asked for.

exit_codes.0: success (the new pull request is on stdout as JSON)
exit_codes.2: invalid input (title is missing, a parameter is wrong, or source and target are the same branch)
exit_codes.4: not permitted (the git repository is above the workspace root)
exit_codes.5: unreachable (DNS failure, connection refused, TLS failure, or the transfer timed out)
exit_codes.6: http error (the API refused: the branch is not pushed, a pull request is already open for it, or the token was refused)
exit_codes.7: no credential (GITHUB_TOKEN is not in this step's environment)
